title: Beyond-Course Opportunity Commissioning and Growth
lead: TBC, Experiential Learning Community of Practice

decisionLog.outcome: Established the working Year 1 commissioning model for 2.2.4 as four distinct year-round packages within a £150,000 investment request: Final-Year Graduate Futures Programme (£65,000), Service and Community-Engaged Experience Programme (£40,000), Belonging and Connection Programme (£25,000), and Responsive Opportunity Commissioning (£20,000). The packages share an annual delivery rhythm, with lighter and more scalable provision earlier in the cycle and greater use of sustained or intensive opportunities where the academic calendar permits, while Belonging and Connection remains predominantly short and active. The model is recorded as working delivery design while the deliverable remains at proposition-development pending stakeholder proposition review.

Confirmed that the 2.2.4 proposition is sufficiently clear and developed to move into informal stakeholder sense-check. Advance planningStatus from proposition-development to proposition-review; open ownership questions and stakeholder feedback will be resolved and recorded during Proposition Review before any move into Delivery Design.

Rebalanced the working Year 1 commissioning portfolio while retaining the £150,000 total investment request and the commitment to at least 2,500 deduplicated unique students. The revised four year-round packages are Final-Year Career Enhancement Programme (£50,000), Entrepreneurship and Enterprise Experience Programme (£40,000), Belonging and Connection Programme (£30,000), and Service and Community-Engaged Experience Programme (£30,000). Indicative package-level reach is approximately 700, 800, 1,500 and 600 unique students respectively, with approximately 26,500 to 33,500 student-hours planned across the portfolio. Responsive commissioning is retained as a principle of the overall commissioning model rather than a separate funding package.

Extended the working investment case from the detailed Year 1 base into a three-year mobilisation trajectory and an enduring business-as-usual model. Annual mobilisation investment rises from £150,000 in Year 1 to £200,000 in Year 2 and £250,000 in Year 3, followed by an indicative steady-state requirement of £175,000 per year. The portfolio ambition grows from at least 2,500 distinct students in Year 1 (around 6% of the current King's student population), to 4,000 in Year 2 (around 9%), 6,500 in Year 3 (around 15%) and around 9,000 at steady state (around 20%). Indicative student-hours rise from 26,500 to 33,500 in Year 1, to 55,000 to 65,000 in Year 2, 100,000 to 115,000 in Year 3 and 145,000 to 165,000 at steady state. Sustained high-intensity places grow from around 350 to 500 to 600 and then plateau at around 600. The scaling model depends on accumulating reusable evergreen courses and projects as low-marginal-cost entry points, using short active experiences to convert reach into meaningful participation, while protecting sustained intensive provision as the deepest and most people-intensive layer.

Clarified the annual delivery model and simplified the delivery timeline. Each annual portfolio will set overarching investment, deduplicated reach, student-hours and depth ambitions, then devolve responsibility for defined contributions to a small number of thematic workpackages whose mix can change from year to year. The detailed Year 1 workpackages remain mapped as the first instance of this model. The timeline will track the evolution of 2.2.4 as a deliverable rather than showing each thematic workpackage as a parallel delivery step, and the £150,000 Year 1 investment will be recorded once at portfolio level to avoid fragmented presentation or double-counting.

Reframed the proposition around its primary student-facing purpose: growing King's supply of substantive learning opportunities beyond the course. Strategic priorities, identified gaps, student need and future-facing evidence from across King's Edge are treated as inputs that shape a responsive annual opportunity portfolio. Commissioning, devolved thematic workpackages and the evergreen/short-active/sustained delivery model are retained as the mechanisms through which that portfolio grows. The five-step timeline has been recast accordingly around translating priorities into the Year 1 portfolio, delivering and learning, refreshing and growing in Year 2, scaling in Year 3 and establishing an enduring opportunity portfolio.

Confirmed that the existing £150,000 / £200,000 / £250,000 commissioning trajectory and its associated benefit ambitions remain the recommended Core source-plan baseline after the wider King's Edge cost rebaseline. Core therefore continues to plan for at least 2,500 / 4,000 / 6,500 distinct students annually, approximately 26,500–33,500 / 55,000–65,000 / 100,000–115,000 student-hours, and around 350 / 500 / 600 sustained high-intensity places across Years 1–3.
decisionLog.notes: Economy and Enhanced benefit ranges are decision-support scenarios held in the portfolio investment handover, not alternative source-plan targets. Scenario modelling should reflect the portfolio's non-linear economics: reusable evergreen provision supports reach at lower marginal cost, while partnership capacity and people-intensive delivery disproportionately affect total student-hours and sustained high-intensity places.

decisionLog.outcome: Clarified the proposed £60,000 pre-business-case release as seed funding against, not additional to, the £150,000 Year 1 new-opportunity commissioning envelope. If released early, the £60,000 may be distributed across the existing thematic workpackages rather than treated as a fifth or separate pot, with a deliberate final-year focus across Careers, Entrepreneurship and Enterprise, and Service and Community-Engaged Experience. The early package should aim to engage around 700 final-year undergraduates, approximately 10% of the graduating undergraduate population, generate approximately 10,000 to 12,000 student-hours and support around 150 sustained places providing internship-like experience, alongside shorter and more scalable new opportunities.
decisionLog.notes: The final-year figures are an early seed-package ambition and a subset of the wider Year 1 portfolio, not an additional population to add to the full-year 2,500-student target. The full Year 1 portfolio remains subject to the substantive mobilisation decision and retains the existing ambition of at least 2,500 distinct students, 26,500–33,500 student-hours and around 350 sustained high-intensity places.
